And if there was no distribution error or noise, it was just perfect, right? In that world, it could make sense that everybody's got it immediately and now it can't really—it can be an offensive tool. But that's not how technology gets deployed, right?
turns.zh: 那关于 Mythos 呢？我的意思是，如果你说，好吧，每个人都能同时获得 Mythos 并立即应用，对吧？如果没有任何分发错误或噪声，它是完美的，对吧？在那种世界里，每个人立即拥有它，它可能成为攻击工具，这或许说得通。但技术不是这样部署的，对吧？

turns.en: Absolutely never do this because they would be sued into oblivion.
turns.zh: 绝对不会这么做，因为他们会被起诉到破产。

turns.en: You mean release—
turns.zh: 你是说发布——

turns.en: Release a dangerous—
turns.zh: 发布一个危险的——

turns.en: I think Anthropic is Mythos. Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我认为 Anthropic 就是 Mythos。是的。是的。

turns.en: If you release a system that can obviously be used for just nefarious uses without any protection, that's negligence. I mean, you would be sued into oblivion.
turns.zh: 如果你发布一个明显可用于恶意用途且没有任何保护的系统，那就是过失。我的意思是，你会被起诉到破产。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And so those companies actually have a pretty good incentive to actually do it right.
turns.zh: 所以那些公司实际上有很好的动机去正确行事。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Now that doesn't mean you don't want explicit regulations for certain aspects of what those systems can do and cannot do.
turns.zh: 但这并不意味着你不想要针对这些系统能做什么和不能做什么的某些方面的明确法规。

turns.en: But that's it because what the argument you just made is similar to like, okay, you expect food companies to make sure that their food is safe and healthy and so on. Now that we know that's not totally true, right?
turns.zh: 但就是这样，因为你刚才的论点类似于，好吧，你期望食品公司确保他们的食品是安全和健康的等等。现在我们知道那并不完全正确，对吧？

turns.en: True. You're right. You're right.
turns.zh: 没错。你说得对。你说得对。

turns.en: Because they will make tradeoffs for the sake of profitability that aren't necessarily in the public interest, right?
turns.zh: 因为他们会为了盈利而做出不一定符合公共利益的权衡，对吧？

turns.en: It's the same in airplane design and—
turns.zh: 飞机设计也是如此——

turns.en: If airplanes start falling out of the sky, it's not good for business.
turns.zh: 如果飞机开始从天上掉下来，那对生意不利。

turns.en: I mean there is the FAA, but there is also—
turns.zh: 我的意思是，有 FAA，但也有——

turns.en: Right, exactly.
turns.zh: 对，没错。

turns.en: There's also private companies that actually certify certain maintenance processes and stuff like that and inspections.
turns.zh: 也有私营公司实际上认证某些维护流程和检查之类的事情。

turns.en: And you think about pharma and the FDA, like it was the Wild West in the early 1900s, people were putting anything out on the market, calling it medicine, people were dying. They had to do something different, right?
turns.zh: 你想想制药和 FDA，就像 20 世纪初的蛮荒时代，人们把任何东西投放市场，称之为药物，人们因此死亡。他们不得不采取不同的做法，对吧？

turns.en: That's what I'm saying. Those regulations already exist. Whether AI is used for those products or not is irrelevant. I mean every technology that's ever been put out has always had a downside and bad side effects, and the question for society is what type of appropriate regulation will preserve the benefits of that technology and minimize the bad side effects?
turns.zh: 这就是我在说的。那些法规已经存在。AI 是否用于那些产品无关紧要。我的意思是，每一项被推出的技术总是有缺点和不良副作用，社会的问题是哪种适当的监管能保留该技术的好处并最小化不良副作用？

turns.en: Mhm. And there is a website that I would recommend people visit because it's educational and hilarious at the same time.
turns.zh: 嗯。有一个网站我推荐人们去看看，因为它既有教育意义又很搞笑。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: It's called the Pessimist Archive.
turns.zh: 它叫“悲观主义者档案”。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: So it's a gentleman who as a hobby basically collects newspaper clips from various periods of history where people have said, oh, this new technology, this new cultural phenomenon, this new communication technology is going to destroy society. And just go back a few years, video games were going to destroy the youth.
turns.zh: 所以是一位先生作为爱好收集历史各个时期的报纸剪报，人们说，哦，这项新技术、这种新文化现象、这种新通信技术将摧毁社会。就退回几年，电子游戏要摧毁青年。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And a few years before that, rock and roll—
turns.zh: 再往前几年，摇滚乐——

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: —and comic books—
turns.zh: ——还有漫画书——

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: —and recorded music and jazz and go back long enough, novels. Novels were going to destroy young women because they would spend their time just reading instead of working in the fields, right? So why do you waste your time reading books?
turns.zh: ——还有录制的音乐和爵士乐，再往前足够久，小说。小说要摧毁年轻女性，因为她们会把时间花在阅读上而不是在田里干活，对吧？所以你为什么要浪费时间读书？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And there's kind of progression depending on your age or your willingness to adopt new things. Was that Plato or Aristotle who said writing was a terrible idea because it would cause people to not have memory anymore?
turns.zh: 而且有一种进展，取决于你的年龄或你接受新事物的意愿。是柏拉图还是亚里士多德说书写是个糟糕的主意，因为它会导致人们不再有记忆？

turns.en: Yeah. It would destroy oral tradition and the ability to think. Yeah, exactly. Build arguments in your head.
turns.zh: 是的。它会摧毁口头传统和思考能力。是的，没错。在头脑中构建论点。

turns.en: So we're going to be careful not to overreact. I mean, there's clearly some areas where it makes sense to regulate.
turns.zh: 所以我们要小心不要过度反应。我的意思是，显然有些领域进行监管是合理的。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: But I think the more general question is what people have been talking about over the last several years is if you think AI is intrinsically dangerous regardless of the application, you should regulate research and development in AI.
turns.zh: 但我认为更普遍的问题是人们过去几年一直在谈论的：如果你认为 AI 本质上是危险的，无论应用如何，你就应该监管 AI 的研究和开发。

turns.en: Mm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And in my opinion, that's obscurantism. That's really—
turns.zh: 而在我看来，那是蒙昧主义。那真的——

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: That makes no sense. I do not believe AI is intrinsically dangerous.
turns.zh: 那毫无道理。我不相信 AI 本质上是危险的。

turns.en: Mm-hmm. And a regulation at the level of development doesn't seem to actually make a lot of sense. I think it's at the level of deployment that there should be some check, right?
turns.zh: 嗯。而且开发层面的监管似乎并不太合理。我认为应该在部署层面有一些检查，对吧？

turns.en: That. Yeah.
turns.zh: 那个。是的。

turns.en: So, is there the larger danger, and I've heard you say this before, maybe just the consolidation of power and compute and data and so on and so forth in a few companies?
turns.zh: 那么，是否有更大的危险，我以前听你说过，也许只是权力、算力和数据等等集中在少数公司手中？

turns.en: Right. That's really dangerous.
turns.zh: 对。那真的很危险。

turns.en: Yeah. And so speak to that a little bit.
turns.zh: 是的。那请稍微谈谈这个。

turns.en: Right. So, more and more we're using AI assistants as our main source of information.
turns.zh: 好的。所以，我们越来越多地使用 AI 助手作为我们的主要信息来源。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So, we rarely go to search engines anymore, right? We rarely go to Wikipedia or to a library or to a primary source of information. We just ask a question and see what comes back.
turns.zh: 所以，我们很少再去搜索引擎了，对吧？我们很少去维基百科或图书馆或一手信息来源。我们只是问一个问题，看看返回什么。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And they come from three or four companies on the west coast of the US or China at the moment.
turns.zh: 而它们目前来自美国西海岸或中国的三四家公司。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: That might be acceptable for some American governments. It is completely unacceptable everywhere else in the world.
turns.zh: 这对某些美国政府来说可能可以接受。在世界其他地方则完全不可接受。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Talk to democratic governments in Western Europe or in Asia.
turns.zh: 跟西欧或亚洲的民主政府谈谈。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: They do not want their citizens to get all of their information diet through AI assistants that are proprietary systems produced in the US.
turns.zh: 他们不希望自己的公民通过美国生产的专有系统的 AI 助手获取全部信息食粮。

turns.en: For sure they don't.
turns.zh: 他们当然不想。

turns.en: Unacceptable. And so they—
turns.zh: 不可接受。所以他们——

turns.en: There's like a cultural sovereignty that's lost, right? And even epistemology—
turns.zh: 就像失去了文化主权，对吧？甚至认识论——

turns.en: Political biases, value systems.
turns.zh: 政治偏见、价值体系。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: I mean, there's a lot of implied value systems in AI systems. They speak certain languages and not others.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，AI 系统中有很多隐含的价值体系。它们说某些语言而不说其他语言。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: They have access to a particular type of data not others. And so there's a lot of underlying values and centers of interest in the current crop of AI systems.
turns.zh: 它们能访问特定类型的数据而不是其他数据。所以当前这批 AI 系统中有很多潜在的价值观和利益中心。

turns.en: And so in my opinion, the only way to fix this is for—I mean, basically foundation models, AI foundation models are quickly becoming an infrastructure. And infrastructure always wants to be open. And so the future of the AI market, if you want, which is completely inevitable—the question is how long it's going to take—is one in which basic foundation models are open and free. And then commercial applications are built on top of it by integrating multiple models, fine-tuning them for vertical applications, making them palatable for the public, having them adopt certain personalities, being fine-tuned for particular cultures and political biases, whatever.
turns.zh: 所以在我看来，解决这个问题的唯一办法是——我的意思是，基础模型，AI 基础模型正迅速成为一种基础设施。而基础设施总是希望开放的。所以 AI 市场的未来，如果你愿意这么说的话，是完全不可避免的——问题只是需要多长时间——那就是基础模型是开放且免费的。然后商业应用建立在其之上，通过集成多个模型、针对垂直应用进行微调、让公众更容易接受、让它们采用某些个性、针对特定文化和政治偏见等进行微调，诸如此类。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。是的。

turns.en: Well, you need a diversity of AI assistants for the same reason you need a diversity of the press. You don't want to get all of your news from a single political philosophy and value system. That's unthinkable for most countries in the world. So that's the future I want to see. It's one in which the expensive part of producing an LLM can be done collaboratively with multiple countries, regions, private companies, etc., in the world to train a sort of global system that would be a repository of all human knowledge. But then because it's open and free, on top of this, private actors can build practical systems on top of them and have a good business from it. That's the future I want to see.
turns.zh: 嗯，你需要多样化的 AI 助手，就像你需要多样化的媒体一样。你不想从单一的政治哲学和价值体系获取所有新闻。这对世界上大多数国家来说是不可想象的。所以这就是我想看到的未来。在这个未来中，生产 LLM 的昂贵部分可以通过与世界上多个国家、地区、私营公司等合作来完成，训练一个全球系统，成为所有人类知识的存储库。但然后因为它是开放和免费的，在此基础上，私营主体可以在它们之上构建实用系统，并从中获得良好的业务。这就是我想看到的未来。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: So I mean it's like these laws that exist in various European countries—I don't know if there is the equivalent in the US—where a printing press cannot discriminate what they print. It's like your internet service provider cannot filter—they have to be a neutral pipe.
turns.zh: 所以我的意思是，就像欧洲各国存在的这些法律——我不知道美国是否有对应法律——印刷机不能歧视它们印刷的内容。就像你的互联网服务提供商不能过滤——它们必须是一个中立的管道。

turns.en: Right. Right. Yeah. And they certainly aren't now. And we don't know how they're being trained or manipulated or how the data is being weighted. I mean we just don't know.
turns.zh: 对。对。是的。而且它们现在肯定不是。我们不知道它们是如何被训练或操纵的，或者数据是如何被加权的。我的意思是我们就是不知道。

turns.en: Well we don't know and they're necessarily biased. It's not for nefarious reasons. It's not because the companies that build them want a particular type of bias. It's just that necessarily you build a system, it's going to have some bias, right? Like every newspaper is going to have some bias in the way they talk about things. And so there is no fix for this. You're never going to have a completely neutral system. And so the only fix is diversity.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们不知道，而且它们必然有偏见。这不是出于邪恶的原因。不是因为构建它们的公司想要某种特定类型的偏见。只是必然地，你构建一个系统，它就会有一些偏见，对吧？就像每份报纸在谈论事情的方式上都会有一些偏见。所以对此没有解决办法。你永远不会有完全中立的系统。所以唯一的解决办法就是多样性。

turns.en: Is diversity.
turns.zh: 就是多样性。

turns.en: You're not going to get diversity unless you have a free foundation model on top of which people can train diverse models. So you need basically foundation model neutrality in the sense that, the same way the printing press—in France for example there is a law that says the printing press cannot choose what they accept to print, first of all, but then the news distributors cannot discriminate either; they have to distribute all the newspapers, magazines. They can't choose because of political—
turns.zh: 你不会得到多样性，除非你有一个免费的基础模型，人们可以在其上训练多样化的模型。所以你需要基本上基础模型的中立性，就像印刷机——例如在法国，有一项法律规定印刷机不能选择它们接受印刷的内容，首先是这样，然后新闻分发商也不能歧视；它们必须分发所有报纸、杂志。它们不能因为政治——

turns.en: We're not going to send this one out, right.
turns.zh: 我们不会发送这个，对吧。

turns.en: Right, they have to be neutral in that respect.
turns.zh: 对，在这方面它们必须保持中立。

turns.en: Is it possible to take the foundation models that have been built so far and somehow open them up to development by other—maybe country stacks—so that other applications can be built on top of them, or will they always have an embedded bias in them?
turns.zh: 是否有可能将迄今为止构建的基础模型以某种方式开放给其他——也许是国家堆栈——进行开发，以便其他应用可以在它们之上构建，或者它们总是会嵌入偏见？

turns.en: They always have an embedded bias, but if you make them open and fine-tunable by anyone, then you make it possible to have a widely highly diverse set of assistants built on top of them. We cannot do this with the models currently produced by OpenAI and Anthropic and Google because they're closed.
turns.zh: 它们总是有嵌入的偏见，但如果你让它们开放并且任何人都可以微调，那么你就有可能在其上构建广泛高度多样化的助手。我们无法对 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 目前生产的模型这样做，因为它们是封闭的。

turns.en: But could they open them or is that not possible to like—
turns.zh: 但它们能开放它们吗，或者那不可能像——

turns.en: Not in their kind of business model, right.
turns.zh: 在它们的商业模式下不行，对吧。

turns.en: They wouldn't allow it because they're—I mean—
turns.zh: 它们不会允许，因为它们——我的意思是——

turns.en: And they want to capture the world.
turns.zh: 而且它们想占领世界。

turns.en: That's right and given the level of investment that they are currently—you know kind of money they're raising—they think that's the only way for them to preserve that business model. Now—
turns.zh: 没错，考虑到它们目前——你知道它们筹集的资金规模——它们认为这是它们保持那种商业模式的唯一方式。现在——

turns.en: It's a sort of a winner-take-all view of the world.
turns.zh: 这是一种赢家通吃的世界观。

turns.en: So the reason that Anthropic and Dario Amodei are saying is again—you know we're not going to open it because it's too dangerous. Like you can't let the unwashed masses have access to such powerful technology—which I think again is obscurantism.
turns.zh: 所以 Anthropic 和 Dario Amodei 说的理由又是——你知道我们不会开放它，因为太危险了。就像你不能让未洗的群众接触如此强大的技术——我认为这又是蒙昧主义。

turns.en: A new form of medieval obscurantism.
turns.zh: 一种新形式的中世纪蒙昧主义。

turns.en: Yeah. Now other companies, the Chinese companies are opening up their models. They're open. And in fact, they're increasingly used for that reason. Now they are biased in some other way initially, but because they are open, they can be fine-tuned to remove that bias or create another bias rather.
turns.zh: 是的。现在其他公司，中国公司正在开放他们的模型。它们是开放的。事实上，正因为如此，它们被越来越多地使用。现在它们最初以某种其他方式有偏见，但因为它们是开放的，可以微调以消除那种偏见，或者更确切地说创建另一种偏见。

turns.en: And they're very popular. They're getting more and more popular.
turns.zh: 而且它们非常受欢迎。它们越来越受欢迎。

turns.en: They're good and they're increasingly popular, but they are Chinese and so there is a little bit of trepidation about—yeah.
turns.zh: 它们很好，而且越来越受欢迎，但它们是中国的，所以有一点不安——是的。

turns.en: You can call it this way.
turns.zh: 你可以这么称呼。

turns.en: Yeah. And certainly they're certainly biased in their models as well because of the whole context in which they're being developed. I don't imagine the companies in China would not—I think—be able to behave the way the companies here are. The Chinese government would not put up with entertaining the idea of loss of control. They wouldn't put up with the idea that these things are dangerous and like I just don't think they'd allow a company to behave like that because the one thing that I know about the Chinese party is control is the one thing that they are going to maintain at all costs.
turns.zh: 是的。而且当然，它们的模型也肯定有偏见，因为整个开发背景。我不认为中国的公司会——我认为——能够像这里的公司那样行事。中国政府不会容忍失去控制的想法。他们不会容忍这些东西很危险的想法，我只是不认为他们会允许一家公司那样行事，因为我对中国党的了解是，控制是他们不惜一切代价要维持的一件事。

turns.en: Yeah, that's true.
turns.zh: 是的，没错。

turns.en: And it's interesting that the Chinese companies are mostly opening up their models because they see it as a way to have visibility in the market. Because the Chinese market in terms of services is really an isolated ecosystem—a way of having an impact around the world.
turns.zh: 有趣的是，中国公司大多开放他们的模型，因为他们将其视为在市场中获得可见性的一种方式。因为中国服务市场确实是一个孤立的生态系统——一种在全世界产生影响的方式。

transcript.sec: Project Tapestry: A Global Foundation Model

turns.en: The business model is still viable for them; they derive enough revenue to justify their existence. And they're doing it at much lower cost as well, because their whole industrial model is to stay slightly behind, right? So they're leveraging the advances that these companies are making. So I think ultimately the solution is—and it's a project that I've advocated for for several years now—it's called Project Tapestry. The idea is that a global foundation model that could be the repository of all human knowledge could be built and trained collaboratively with partners that can be countries or regions or universities or private companies collaborating to train a global system, using a form of training procedure that does not require each participant to share their data. So there are techniques by which you can train a model where each participant contributes data and compute but they keep control of their data. They don't share their data.
turns.zh: 他们的商业模式仍然可行；他们获得的收入足以证明其存在的合理性。而且他们以低得多的成本做到这一点，因为他们的整个产业模式就是保持稍微落后，对吧？所以他们正在利用这些公司取得的进步。所以我认为最终的解决方案是——这是我多年来一直倡导的一个项目——它叫做 Project Tapestry。这个想法是，一个可以成为所有人类知识库的全球基础模型，可以由合作伙伴协作构建和训练，这些合作伙伴可以是国家、地区、大学或私营公司，共同训练一个全球系统，使用一种不需要每个参与者共享数据的训练程序。所以有一些技术可以让你训练一个模型，每个参与者贡献数据和算力，但他们保持对自己数据的控制。他们不共享数据。

turns.en: So it's like zero-knowledge data? Like it's their own data, training on their data, but it's never distributed. It always keeps belonging to them.
turns.zh: 所以这就像零知识数据？就像这是他们自己的数据，在他们的数据上训练，但数据永远不会被分发。它始终属于他们。

turns.en: Never made publicly available. It's never shared with the other participants. What those participants share are parameter vectors. So basically the big list of numbers that define the model, right? And when they train on their own data, they periodically exchange their parameter vectors with the other participants, and the system eventually arrives at a consensus parameter vector that is as good as if you had trained a single system on all the data from all the participants. They don't exchange their data. So they keep control and sovereignty over their data. And in my opinion, there is a lot of data in the world that is currently not publicly available, not usable, or maybe not even digitized, which if it were used in that way, would produce models that are actually better than the commercial systems.
turns.zh: 永远不会公开。它永远不会与其他参与者共享。参与者共享的是参数向量。基本上就是定义模型的那一大串数字，对吧？当他们用自己的数据训练时，他们会定期与其他参与者交换参数向量，系统最终会达成一个共识参数向量，其效果与在所有参与者的所有数据上训练单个系统一样好。他们不交换数据。所以他们保持对自己数据的控制权和主权。在我看来，世界上有很多数据目前没有公开、无法使用，甚至可能没有数字化，如果以这种方式使用，会产生实际上比商业系统更好的模型。

turns.en: Yeah. And a big chunk of what makes the quality of an AI system is the post-training, which is asking the system questions and then giving it the answer or rating the answer it produces. They can be crowdsourced across the world. Kind of like a little bit like a former Wikipedia, but instead of writing articles about particular topics, you just train an AI system to answer questions or produce information about particular topics.
turns.zh: 是的。而决定 AI 系统质量的一大部分是后训练，也就是向系统提问，然后给出答案或对系统产生的答案进行评分。这些可以在全球范围内众包。有点像以前的维基百科，但不是撰写关于特定主题的文章，而是训练 AI 系统回答关于特定主题的问题或产生信息。

turns.en: This Tapestry idea would be a way to actually get a lot of this data off the sidelines and sort of make it—to have an open system trained on all the world's languages with all the world's value systems and biases and whatever you want to call them.
turns.zh: 这个 Tapestry 想法将是一种实际上让很多数据从场外发挥作用的方式，并使其——拥有一个在所有世界语言、所有世界价值体系和偏见以及任何你想称呼它们的东西上训练的开源系统。

turns.en: Without violating data privacy.
turns.zh: 而不侵犯数据隐私。

turns.en: Without violating ownership of data from countries. So you know, India has 22 official languages and literally hundreds of local languages and dialects, even more dialects. Like who's going to train a model that speaks all those languages? Do you think it's going to be trained by Anthropic, OpenAI, or anyone else? Like they don't even have the data for it. But India can build the data for that.
turns.zh: 而不侵犯国家对数据的所有权。所以你知道，印度有 22 种官方语言，还有数百种地方语言和方言，甚至更多方言。谁来训练一个会说所有这些语言的模型？你认为会由 Anthropic、OpenAI 或其他任何人来训练吗？他们甚至没有这方面的数据。但印度可以为此构建数据。

turns.en: Yeah. And they are actually, I think, they're going to build their own stack.
turns.zh: 是的。而且我认为他们实际上会构建自己的技术栈。

turns.en: Well, they have an effort called Bharat Gen which basically is that. But then why should they not collaborate with Vietnam that has the same problem, or Indonesia that has the same problem, or Korea or Japan or France or Germany or every other country in the world or Kazakhstan? And so all of those countries will have invested interest in participating in a program like this.
turns.zh: 嗯，他们有一个叫做 Bharat Gen 的努力，基本上就是这个。但那么他们为什么不与有同样问题的越南、有同样问题的印度尼西亚、韩国、日本、法国、德国或世界上所有其他国家或哈萨克斯坦合作呢？所以所有这些国家都会有投资兴趣参与这样的项目。

turns.en: Well, it seems like the interest right now among nation states—the big concern when you talk to political leaders is sovereignty. That's a big one, which is really difficult to accomplish, not just because of the closed model thing, but just because it's impossible to create a sovereign stack. It really is. It's not just at the frontier model level—frontier models being part of the problem—but this winner-take-all approach that these companies seem to be pursuing certainly puts them in a position of being very concerned about whether or not there is going to be sovereignty going forward, because a super powerful AI that everybody is using doesn't bode well for countries or nation states.
turns.zh: 嗯，目前民族国家之间的兴趣似乎——当你与政治领导人交谈时，最大的担忧是主权。这是一个大问题，而且真的很难实现，不仅仅是因为闭源模型的问题，而是因为创建主权技术栈是不可能的。确实如此。这不仅仅是在前沿模型层面——前沿模型是问题的一部分——而是这些公司似乎正在追求的这种赢家通吃的方法，确实让他们非常担心未来是否会有主权，因为一个所有人都在使用的超级强大的 AI 对国家或民族国家来说不是好兆头。

turns.en: Right. So I mean there's a future that I think we can all live with. There's an interesting parallel also in history. If you go back to the early days of the internet, if you wanted to put together an internet service of any kind, you had to buy computers from Sun Microsystems, Hewlett Packard, Dell or one of those, which would run proprietary operating systems based on Unix or Windows. And on top of this you would have a proprietary software stack. That lasted only a few years. After a few years this was completely wiped out and replaced by commodity hardware, open source operating systems—Linux mostly—and then completely open source stack on top of it: Apache, MySQL, PHP. And most websites and internet services were built with this. Facebook was built with PHP on top of Linux and Apache.
turns.zh: 对。所以我的意思是，有一个我认为我们都能接受的未来。历史上也有一个有趣的平行。如果你回到互联网的早期，如果你想搭建任何类型的互联网服务，你必须从 Sun Microsystems、惠普、戴尔或类似公司购买计算机，这些计算机会运行基于 Unix 或 Windows 的专有操作系统。在此基础上，你还会有一个专有软件栈。这只持续了几年。几年后，这被完全淘汰，被商品硬件、开源操作系统（主要是 Linux）以及其上的完全开源栈（Apache、MySQL、PHP）所取代。大多数网站和互联网服务都是用这些构建的。Facebook 是用 PHP 在 Linux 和 Apache 之上构建的。

turns.en: So you can privatize at the level of the application layer, just not the infrastructure layer.
turns.zh: 所以你可以在应用层进行私有化，只是不能在基础设施层。

turns.en: Infrastructure really wants to be open because it's more secure, it's cheaper, it's portable, and it creates the landscape and the substrate for a vibrant industry. I saw that effect at Meta in 2023 where when Meta open sourced Llama 2, this completely jump-started the AI industry. It made people realize, oh, now we have an open source model we can fine-tune for anything we want. Llama 3 was great.
turns.zh: 基础设施确实希望开放，因为它更安全、更便宜、更便携，并且为充满活力的行业创造了景观和基础。我在 2023 年在 Meta 看到了这种效果，当 Meta 开源 Llama 2 时，这完全启动了 AI 行业。它让人们意识到，哦，现在我们有了一个开源模型，我们可以针对任何我们想要的东西进行微调。Llama 3 很棒。

transcript.sec: Meta's Open Stance and NVIDIA's Moves

turns.en: Llama 4 was not so great, so disappointed a lot of people and then caused Mark Zuckerberg to completely reboot AI at Meta and for one year Meta kind of stopped adopting this sort of open stance and now it's coming back to it.
turns.zh: Llama 4 表现不太好，让很多人失望，然后导致马克·扎克伯格在 Meta 彻底重启 AI，有一年时间 Meta 差不多停止了采取这种开放立场，现在又回归了。

turns.en: Which I think is a really good evolution. We see kind of a similar move towards openness from NVIDIA with, you know, they bought Hugging Face.
turns.zh: 我觉得这是一个很好的演变。我们看到 NVIDIA 也有类似的开放举措，你知道，他们收购了 Hugging Face。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: They're partnering with Mistral in the Nemotron consortium which also has some open source.
turns.zh: 他们与 Mistral 在 Nemotron 联盟中合作，该联盟也有一些开源项目。

turns.en: Towards an open model as well?
turns.zh: 也走向开放模型？

turns.en: I think NVIDIA has like a vested interest in the ecosystem being open. They need more actors, right? They sell GPUs to all of them, so
turns.zh: 我认为 NVIDIA 在生态系统开放方面有既得利益。他们需要更多的参与者，对吧？他们向所有人销售 GPU，所以

turns.en: Yeah. They have the most to gain.
turns.zh: 是的。他们获益最大。

turns.en: Better for them to have a wide diversity of clients rather than like three.
turns.zh: 对他们来说，拥有广泛的客户多样性比只有三个客户要好。

turns.en: Right. But ultimately this sort of tapestry has to be like owned by a nonprofit foundation. Possibly with commercial outfits on top of it.
turns.zh: 对。但最终这种格局必须由非营利基金会拥有。可能上面还有商业机构。

transcript.sec: Incentives for Closed Models and National Security

turns.en: So there's obviously incentive inside the company to say that the models are dangerous and therefore this captive closed model approach is the right one. It seems like that is the fact that these companies are now also very involved in national security and there's been this sort of increasing collaboration, I guess you could say, between the national security apparatus and the military industrial complex and these companies would seem to be like feeding into this idea that these have to be controlled closed systems and we would also have an incentive to ensure that they are the systems that are used most globally. And it's a terrible combination of factors, but it seems like what I worry about is that currently the US government is inclined to actually keep them closed because of the national security implications, I guess.
turns.zh: 所以公司内部显然有动机说模型是危险的，因此这种封闭的专属模型方法是正确的。看起来事实是，这些公司现在也非常参与国家安全，而且国家安全机构和军工复合体之间的合作越来越多，这些公司似乎在助长这种观念：这些必须是受控的封闭系统，我们也有动机确保它们是在全球使用最多的系统。这是一个糟糕的因素组合，但我担心的是，目前美国政府倾向于因为国家安全影响而实际上保持它们封闭。

transcript.secZh: 封闭模型的激励与国家安全

turns.en: So strangely enough, you hear people like Alex Karp, the CEO of Palantir, actually advocating for a more open ecosystem. You know, he doesn't like the idea of having just a few proprietary systems controlled by a few companies. He thinks that's actually counterproductive. There are arguments on both sides of the political spectrum in the US in favor and against open model. So a lot of people on the hawkish conservative side saying, you know, this is sort of revealing our secrets to the Chinese. And people also on the more progressive liberal side also you know
turns.zh: 所以奇怪的是，你会听到像 Palantir 的 CEO 亚历克斯·卡普这样的人实际上倡导更开放的生态系统。你知道，他不喜欢只有少数专有系统由少数公司控制的想法。他认为那实际上适得其反。美国政治光谱两边都有支持和反对开放模型的论点。所以很多鹰派保守派说，你知道，这有点像是向中国泄露我们的秘密。而更进步的自由派人士也，你知道

turns.en: Be quite hawkish also.
turns.zh: 也相当鹰派。

turns.en: Okay, but there are people like Eric Schmidt who basically completely changed his stance on it. He was kind of a little bit opposed to open source because he said like that's giving our best secret to the Chinese. But then DeepSeek happened. He said like okay, the Chinese are you know at the same level, they're really good like you know we're shooting ourselves in the foot by not having open source. So he's now a big supporter of open source models. He's actually funding a few open source project LLM projects academic mostly, but yeah. So and he's very much you know interested in all issues of defense and geopolitics.
turns.zh: 好吧，但像埃里克·施密特这样的人基本上完全改变了他的立场。他之前有点反对开源，因为他说那会把我们最好的秘密给中国。但后来 DeepSeek 出现了。他说好吧，中国人和我们水平相当，他们真的很棒，你知道，我们不搞开源是在自掘坟墓。所以他现在是开源模型的大力支持者。他实际上资助了几个开源项目，主要是学术界的 LLM 项目，但没错。所以他非常关心国防和地缘政治的所有问题。

turns.en: Very involved. He's been for a long time.
turns.zh: 非常参与。他长期以来一直如此。

turns.en: Yeah, so he totally changes his stance on it. And surprisingly enough, there is actually quite some support from the Trump administration for open models.
turns.zh: 是的，所以他完全改变了立场。令人惊讶的是，特朗普政府实际上相当支持开放模型。

turns.en: I don't agree with basically anything from the Trump administration, but they
turns.zh: 我基本上不同意特朗普政府的任何东西，但他们

turns.en: But on this
turns.zh: 但在这点上

turns.en: So on this, I have to say they are on the right side of history. And you know, one reason a lot of people in Silicon Valley got scared before the election, you know, by some rumors about what the Democratic Party attitude towards AI was because of talks of regulation, you know, from the idea that that would have basically made open source models illegal. And there were proposals of laws in California SB 1047 and various proposals in the Biden administration for regulation that spooked a lot of people in Silicon Valley.
turns.zh: 所以在这点上，我不得不说他们站在历史正确的一边。你知道，硅谷很多人在大选前感到害怕的一个原因是，有一些关于民主党对 AI 态度的传言，因为监管的讨论，你知道，那种想法基本上会让开源模型非法。加州有 SB 1047 等法律提案，拜登政府也有各种监管提案，这让硅谷很多人感到不安。

turns.en: I actually gave a I was in front of the Senate subcommittee on intelligence talking about those issues, exactly that issue, like you know, is it dangerous to open source? Should we shoot ourselves in the foot by banning open source? And that was my argument that the vibrancy and vitality of the research and development ecosystem in the US is due to openness. And if we go closed, we're actually going to fall behind.
turns.zh: 实际上我曾在参议院情报小组委员会面前谈论这些问题，正是那个问题，比如，开源危险吗？我们是否应该通过禁止开源来自掘坟墓？我的论点是，美国研发生态系统的活力和生命力源于开放。如果我们走向封闭，我们实际上会落后。

turns.en: Well, thank you. Thank you for sharing the idea and thank you for sharing this hour with me.
turns.zh: 好的，谢谢。谢谢你分享这些想法，也谢谢你与我共度这一小时。

turns.en: Pleasure.
turns.zh: 荣幸。

turns.en: All right. Thanks, Yann.
turns.zh: 好的。谢谢，Yann。

tldr.en: Intelligence is adaptability, not memorized text; LLMs lack true reasoning and planning.
tldr.zh: 智能是适应能力，而非记忆文本；大语言模型缺乏真正的推理与规划。

tldr.en: World models and JEPA enable prediction and planning, essential for human-level intelligence.
tldr.zh: 世界模型与 JEPA 实现预测和规划，是实现人类水平智能的关键。

tldr.en: Open foundation models are safer and more innovative; regulate applications, not R&D.
tldr.zh: 开放基础模型更安全、更具创新性；应监管应用，而非研发。
